checks: The support gap on a row with target p changes by at most the Hausdorff error. On any affected input row it changes by at most a_p times the error, because the excluded-target representation cannot contain p as both input and target. Rows not incident to p stay unchanged.

Linearity in convex coefficients extends the extreme-row inequalities to each excluded-target representation. Grouping lifted generators by base and removing self-weight proves exact prescribed fibers. Projection remains conv(P), whose integer census is P.

The d-fold vertex systems for perturbed facet planes remain nonsingular and each opposite vertex remains strictly on the inward side. Their resulting d+1 affinely independent points give exactly the simplex cut out by those planes, since the signed defining forms are positive multiples of the corresponding inward barycentric forms.

With original outward unit normal n_i, the signed normal displacement of an old relative-interior facet point solves s=t ψ_i(x+s n_i), so the velocity is ψ_i(x). This applies in both signs and for endpoint facets in d=1. The paths are Hausdorff-continuous and fit the localized margin.
Compared 00208e2b45f0da1a §1. The frozen proof retains the incident-row hypothesis and imposes no strictness on unchanged rows.

overlap.comparison: Its strictness at every extreme row allows simultaneous independent changes of all fibers. The present result needs only incident-row strictness for a chosen fiber, so unrelated rows may be tight, and explicitly realizes affine simplex facet velocities.
The accepted result varies ambient polytope rows jointly and computes the resulting owner speeds. It does not give this independent one-fiber motion criterion.

readability: The arbitrary positive gap in the empty incident-row case is harmless, and the common conclusion is about actual convex hull fibers.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: Strictness only on extreme anchored rows incident to the chosen fiber gives actual free motion at that fiber and realizes independent affine facet velocities for a simplex.
